## 2026-09-25 — Elapsed time, not mandatory game-second ticks

Accepted clock conversion independently of integration and rendering cadence: 1x remains one real second per game minute, but does not require 60 whole-world steps. The finite integrator captures starting work/rates and advances to mechanical deadlines or explicit base-world fidelity bounds. This reverses the earlier fixed-second optimization constraint while preserving collision, private evidence, conserved inputs, durable command boundaries and honest unpaid time. [Simulation time](simulation-time.md), [base fidelity](worlds/base/time.md) and [PF13](maintainers/performance.md#pf13--elapsed-time-simulation) own the current contract/delivery; [observations](verification/simulation-cadence.md) distinguish measured throughput from outstanding responsiveness/GPU/soak acceptance.

The [running boundary catalogue](maintainers/simulation-boundaries.md) captures natural expirations, conservative proofs, invalidators and unsupported couplings without introducing a universal scheduler. [RP03](maintainers/revisitable-policies.md#rp03--base-world-integration-fidelity) records when the current fidelity should be revisited. Rendering remains device-cadence; a possible 20 Hz pose feed is not a frame cap. The [speech handoff](maintainers/speech-time-integration.md) preserves the independently implemented graded audio, batching and real-time caption policy. Guidance from `fdcbd31` was incorporated by a clean connector rebase; work continues on `feature/simulation-cadence` without rewriting the preserved spatial branch or merging main.

## Elapsed integration

The [simulation-time owner](simulation-time.md#native-interval-contract) resolves due status transitions before capturing rate predicates, applies those already-active rates over a bounded interval and reconciles the endpoint before later time. Numeric comparisons, daily-window edges and reactivation deadlines can shorten an interval. An endpoint activation receives no earlier elapsed duration. The base world retains an explicit fallback for unsupported coupled clamps; the [policy](worlds/base/time.md#physiology-and-effects) and PF13 own that limit, not a hidden universal one-second status tick. The existing effect mutation owner remains the only path to changes and emitted consequences.

Preserve the accepted [elapsed-time contract](simulation-time.md), deterministic input ordering and saved randomness while reducing repeated work. Clock conversion is not a mandatory integration frequency. The implemented finite native loop compiles sorted participant IDs once per `advanceWorld` call, before draft traversal, and reuses them across its boundary-limited intervals. Only actors, animals and heat sources participate; inert scenery is not sorted or proxied at every interval. Nested plan-command transitions refresh the roster before the next native phase. This is valid because current native stepping changes state, not entity membership or actor/animal/heat components. A future native spawning or component-changing family must refresh that roster at its mutation boundary. IDs, not draft entities, cross draft replacement. With no living memory-capable observer, the encounter phase has no work; otherwise perception runs at the accepted interval boundary, with the base world's explicit displacement fidelity. Due actions and rate changes must split integration; batching is not permission to skip meaningful effects.
- Advance elapsed time through the shared bounded-interval owner. Starting-state rates/work and exact action/deadline boundaries replace the old one-second loop; this is an accepted behavior change, not a claim of identical old sampled traces. Never implement elapsed time by scaling one old step and applying endpoint-created work retroactively. Future local schedules need their own dependency and intermediate-effect qualification.
Native throughput must cover the requested elapsed game time with headroom for commands, persistence and publication; it does not require 60 transitions at 1× or 480 at 8×. Measure actual progress, interval count/size, boundary causes and host blocking separately. A faster timer cannot compensate for excessive work in an atomic interval. Establish an immutable snapshot boundary that lets finalization skip unchanged retained branches; preserve mutable seed/migration workflows, append lineage and privacy invalidation. Measure both initial freezing and steady-state growth, rather than counting only a short pre-frozen run.
Action acceptance and first visible movement are different milestones. A 250 ms native timer can delay the first changed position even after a fast command commit. After CPU reduction, evaluate a 50 ms native/replication cadence during active movement, integrating only elapsed game time actually owed. Retain independent one-second routine durability and coalesced optional publications. This is a scheduling change, not permission to advance future time or multiply per-tick database queries. Adopt it only if the movement latency gain survives the increased timer/projection overhead; client prediction remains the separate network-latency option.
This is the accepted optimization direction, not a declaration that dense 8x performance has passed. PF12 sequences wider scaling work; PF13 owns the accepted elapsed-time cutover. Both reuse existing PF/SW/EPR owners. [Rebase and runtime evidence](verification/spatial-rebase-eightx.md) records the measured starting point.
The host converts elapsed time at 60 game seconds per real second: 8x requests **480 game seconds per real second**, not 480 ticks. [Simulation time](simulation-time.md) owns the boundary-limited integration contract. The former 2.08 ms allowance per mandatory game-second step was an unnecessary implementation constraint, not a requirement. At a 50 ms wake, 8x normally offers about 24 game seconds; an idle scene can integrate that in one interval, while a mechanical deadline or fidelity bound can split it. Retain the approximately 8 ms cooperative work budget and measure individual interval overruns; a sparse cadence does not guarantee low tail latency.
Use the starter scene, the current 318-entity sensing workload, and the earlier combined 329-entity/23-surface workload as initial reproducible cases, not population limits or a promise that every spatial distribution passes. Independently vary history, observer count, moving targets, sounds, profile count, stacked floors, render coverage and geometry edits. The original rebase evidence recorded a dense 8x failure under one-second stepping. [Elapsed-time observations](verification/simulation-cadence.md) record the new short runs separately; they do not establish long-session, arbitrary-density or physical-GPU capacity.
Do not cap heard speech, drop visibility entries, sleep an offscreen actor, shorten sensory range, or jump over a required action/rate/deadline boundary to meet the target. The accepted elapsed-time integration deliberately replaces the old fixed-second sampling; its explicit perception approximation is owned by [base time fidelity](worlds/base/time.md), not disguised as exact continuous observation. The current straight-line acoustic family remains intentionally simpler than diffraction/reverberation; a new room-acoustic model is not a prerequisite for optimizing it.
The rebased host already has bounded routine persistence, frozen snapshots, append-aware history, bounded-interval yielding and trigger-based background work. Reuse them rather than adding a second journal or another universal queue. Profile applicability/deadline indexes for status effects and active component families; inert props must not repeatedly traverse rules that cannot apply to them. Indefinite sleep/needs/wake effects still advance semantically.

Move genuinely cold historical data off repeated finalization/serialization paths under PF08 while retaining evidence, stable IDs, pending commitments, current knowledge and explicit durable reads. Current constant-rate and finite-work families integrate elapsed time up to known boundaries. Unsupported coupled clamps retain an explicit fallback. More aggressive per-entity/region scheduling and analytical dormant systems remain catalogue candidates requiring their own dependency, conservation and intermediate-event evidence; do not silently skip interactions in active scenes.

Required pending navigation is a **technical simulation barrier**: game time does not advance while a valid current action awaits geometry/route preparation, and that real wait is counted separately instead of being charged to hunger or creating catch-up debt. The service releases its mutation lane while the worker runs; cancellation, pause, restore, preference changes and reads remain available. Existing admitted time debt is preserved; after preparation the normal boundary-limited interval order resumes. This single-world barrier favors deterministic early-game fairness; scheduling independent regions is future work, not a second clock added now. Startup prewarming without a pending action does not freeze the world.
Same-version saves retain XYZ/support, pending/accepted route actions, replan state, native flight/fall and player reveal settings through existing owners. Rebuild disposable worker meshes and collision data on load; rotate timeline/command epochs and reopen paused. Existing development worlds follow the in-place update policy in [Save/load](save-and-load.md#active-development-policy); unsupported unsafe conversions fail explicitly without resetting or replacing a world. [SW](maintainers/spatial-world.md) owns deferred requirements and [verification](verification/recast-integration.md) distinguishes application observations and stress samples from automated qualification.
Ground clicks send movement intentions directly. Native commands and timer transitions share the `WorldService` mutation queue. Explicit commands await repository commit before their results return; routine simulation retains its one-real-second flush policy. Background thought admission and maintenance no longer hold the native timer. The [elapsed-time integrator](simulation-time.md) resolves due starts, captures rates/work, advances to a mechanical/fidelity boundary and commits endpoint effects. Catch-up accepts actual elapsed prefixes and releases mutation ownership before yielding after about eight milliseconds of work; one expensive atomic interval can still exceed that budget.

## Elapsed-time simulation

`temporal-boundaries.ts` composes the current finite native families; `simulation-time.ts` supplies numeric/condition bounds, and `worlds/base/time.ts` owns the bundled horizon and spatial fidelity. `advanceWorld` returns a bounded prefix; the service subtracts actual `simTime` progress. Work/rate predicates are captured at the start, then completion, expiry and perception run at the endpoint. Closed-form falling and saved wander timer remainders do not depend on a compulsory one-second cadence. Static object exposure caches retain only geometry-dependent IDs under immutable dependencies. The [time contract](simulation-time.md), [base policy](worlds/base/time.md), [PF13](maintainers/performance.md#pf13--elapsed-time-simulation) and [runtime evidence](verification/simulation-cadence.md) distinguish delivered finite integration from future local schedules and exact exposure-crossing work. Renderer frame cadence remains independent; this change neither caps it at 20 FPS nor establishes GPU performance.

The application offers owed elapsed game time on its 50 ms wake cadence; the domain chooses boundary-limited intervals instead of one transition per game second. Routine progress is published through the existing host and routine durability remains coalesced to one real second. Explicit commands/control changes commit immediately; clean shutdown flushes pending progress. An abrupt crash can lose the most recent unflushed routine progress. The renderer interpolates committed positions and has no physics authority. The base rate is 60 simulated seconds per real second; 0.5×, 1×, 3× and 8× multiply it. At 1×, one real second is one game minute and a day takes 24 real minutes. The host detects suspension from gaps of more than two seconds between timer callbacks, including callbacks while a batch is busy. Continuous busy time accumulates debt instead of triggering suspension. Each batch accepts a prefix of elapsed intervals after about eight milliseconds of native work, retaining the remainder for follow-up batches after yielding to the event loop and releasing mutation ownership between batches. A single atomic interval can exceed the budget. Speed changes retain admitted simulation debt; pause/resume and genuine suspension reset it. Missing-callback intervals remain excluded from catch-up. Domain transitions use isolated Immer drafts with unchanged branches shared. The server explicitly deep-freezes loaded/migrated state, accepted command/editor snapshots and each native-interval result; freezing skips already-frozen branches. Domain builders remain mutable until server handoff, and auto-freezing remains disabled for compatibility. Domain callers must not mutate a returned snapshot. This avoids whole-world cloning and lets persistence/projection skip unchanged branches; changed collections still require traversal, so this is not a large-population performance claim.
One actor-selected frontier contains at most eight ordered physical steps, each carrying a server-bound native command and its actual disposition. It may exist without a goal. Enqueue preserves existing physical work; explicit replacement/cancellation follows native cancellation without refunding consumed inputs. One ready plan step starts per actor at an interval start, after native emergency handling. Its later work receives only time after that start. Later steps wait for successful native completion and recheck live prerequisites through `executeCommand`. An interruption or failure blocks the frontier and records one private internal experience; it cannot repeatedly execute the remaining steps. Goal pause/termination prevents future dispatch and does not undo already-started work. The last 32 retired step receipts supplement normal durable history. No model call occurs inside continuation.

- [ ] Preserve deterministic candidate/recipient ordering, sense formulas and occurrence-time evidence under the accepted [elapsed-time contract](../simulation-time.md). Intervals stop at required mechanical boundaries; the base world's sampled exposure fidelity is explicit. Do not manufacture a speedup by skipping recipients or backdating emissions to one coarse endpoint.
